Padimate A is predicted to interact with DNA polymerase alpha subunit B, which in turn is targeted by Fenchol, exo-, and ultimately targets Acyl-CoA hydrolase. This pathway implies a possible mechanism by which Padimate A may influence Acyl-CoA hydrolase activity, possibly through modulation of DNA polymerase alpha subunit B. The scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction and functional role of Padimate A in Acyl-CoA hydrolase regulation. The evidence highlights a potential biochemical pathway involving multiple targets, underscoring the complexity of drug-target interactions in this context.
